citizenship.heroTitle: Turkish Citizenship by Real Estate Investment
citizenship.heroSubtitle: HADARA provides trusted, end-to-end guidance for international investors seeking Turkish citizenship through property investment.
citizenship.introText: Türkiye grants citizenship to foreign investors who buy real estate worth at least $400,000 and keep it for a minimum of three years. Your spouse and children under 18 are included in the same application, there is no requirement to live in Türkiye, and you can keep your current nationality.
citizenship.introText2: HADARA guides you through every stage — choosing an eligible property from our projects, the valuation, payment and title deed, then the citizenship file prepared with our legal partners — so the process stays clear and on schedule.
citizenship.requirementsSubtitle: The main conditions a real estate investment must meet to qualify for Turkish citizenship.

requirements.title: Minimum value of $400,000
requirements.desc: The property must be worth at least USD 400,000, or the equivalent in another foreign currency. The amount can be reached with a single property or with several properties together.

requirements.title: Official valuation report
requirements.desc: An appraisal company licensed by the Capital Markets Board (SPK) values the property, and the value in its report must meet the threshold.

requirements.title: Payment in foreign currency
requirements.desc: The price is paid by bank transfer in foreign currency, converted at a Turkish bank against a Foreign Currency Purchase Certificate (DAB) that proves the investment.

requirements.title: Three-year holding commitment
requirements.desc: An annotation is added to the title deed stating that the property will not be sold for at least three years.

requirements.title: Certificate of Conformity
requirements.desc: Once the purchase is registered, the Land Registry issues a Certificate of Conformity confirming that the investment meets the program's conditions.

requirements.title: Off-plan homes qualify
requirements.desc: Homes under construction are also eligible through a notarised promise-to-sell agreement carrying the same three-year commitment.

citizenship.rulesNote: The figures on this page reflect the rules in force at the time of writing and may change. Our team confirms the current requirements before any purchase.
citizenship.stepsSubtitle: Most steps can be handled through a power of attorney, so a short visit to Istanbul is usually enough.

steps.title: Free consultation
steps.desc: We discuss your goals, budget and family members, and shortlist eligible projects and units.

steps.title: Property selection and reservation
steps.desc: Visit in person or by live video, choose your unit and secure it with a reservation agreement.

steps.title: Tax number and bank account
steps.desc: We help you obtain a Turkish tax number and open a local bank account, both needed for the purchase.

steps.title: Valuation and payment
steps.desc: The licensed valuation report is prepared and the price is transferred in foreign currency, with the DAB certificate issued by the bank.

steps.title: Title deed
steps.desc: Ownership is registered at the Land Registry with the three-year annotation — or, for off-plan homes, the notarised promise-to-sell agreement is signed.

steps.title: Certificate of Conformity
steps.desc: The Land Registry reviews the file and issues the Certificate of Conformity for the citizenship application.

steps.title: Residence permit and application
steps.desc: You and your family obtain residence permits, and the citizenship application is submitted with the full set of documents.

steps.title: Approval, ID card and passport
steps.desc: After the authorities' review, the citizenship decision is issued and you apply for your Turkish ID cards and passports.

citizenship.stepsNote: From the title deed to the decision, the process usually takes a few months, depending on the authorities' review.
citizenship.documentsSubtitle: Our team prepares the file with you and checks every document before submission.
documents: Valid passports for the applicant, spouse and children
Birth certificates showing the parents' names
Title deed (or notarised promise-to-sell agreement), valuation report and DAB certificate
citizenship.documentsNote: Documents issued abroad need an apostille (or consular legalisation) and a sworn Turkish translation.
citizenship.costsSubtitle: Besides the property price, budget for the following. We prepare a detailed estimate for your case.

costs.title: Title deed fee

costs.title: Valuation report

costs.title: Translations and notary
costs.desc: Sworn translations and notarisation of passports, certificates and powers of attorney.

costs.title: Official fees
costs.desc: Residence permit, application and passport fees for each family member.

costs.title: Legal support
costs.desc: Fees of the lawyers who prepare and follow the citizenship file.

citizenship.routesSubtitle: Real estate is the most popular route, but the program also accepts these investments.

routes.title: Bank deposit
routes.desc: Kept in a Turkish bank for at least three years.

routes.title: Government bonds
routes.desc: Turkish government debt instruments held for at least three years.

routes.title: Investment funds
routes.desc: Shares in real estate or venture capital investment funds, held for at least three years.

routes.title: Fixed capital investment
routes.desc: An investment in a business, confirmed by the Ministry of Industry and Technology.

routes.title: Employment
routes.desc: Creating jobs for at least 50 people, confirmed by the Ministry of Labour.

citizenship.routesNote: HADARA specialises in the real estate route; for the others we refer you to trusted partners.
citizenship.residenceText: If citizenship is not your goal right now, buying a home in Türkiye also entitles you to a renewable residence permit.

residence.title: From $200,000 in Istanbul
residence.desc: The property must be worth at least USD 200,000 in metropolitan cities such as Istanbul, and USD 100,000 in other provinces.

residence.title: Renewable
residence.desc: The permit is issued for a set period and can be renewed for as long as you own the property.

residence.title: For your family
residence.desc: Your spouse and children under 18 can obtain residence permits as well.

residence.title: Address check
residence.desc: Some neighbourhoods are closed to new residence registrations for foreigners, so we check the address before you buy.

benefits: Visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to over 110 countries
Citizenship for your spouse and children under 18
No residency requirement before or after approval
Dual citizenship is permitted for most nationalities
The right to live, work and study in Türkiye, with access to public healthcare and education
Eligibility to apply for the US E-2 investor visa, as Türkiye is a treaty country
Lifelong citizenship that passes on to your future children
A real asset in Istanbul that can earn rental income and grow in value

faq.heroSubtitle: Answers to the questions we hear most often about HADARA, investing in Turkish real estate, and Turkish citizenship by investment.

items.a: HADARA Real Estate is a boutique real estate development and investment company founded in 2014, headquartered in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul. We design, build and deliver residential and mixed-use developments and private villas across Beylikdüzü and Büyükçekmece.

items.q: What types of projects does HADARA develop?
items.a: Our portfolio spans master-planned residential communities, mixed-use developments combining residences, offices and retail, and bespoke luxury villas — each built with quality construction and long-term value in mind.
All of our current developments are located on Istanbul's European side, in the fast-growing districts of Beylikdüzü, Büyükçekmece, Avcılar and Şişli.

items.q: How can I get in touch with HADARA's team?
items.a: You can reach us through the Contact page, by phone at +90 531 930 92 14, or by email at info@byhadara.com. Our team is available Monday–Saturday, 09:00–18:00 (Istanbul time).

items.q: Why invest in real estate in Istanbul?
items.a: Istanbul combines a growing economy, expanding infrastructure and strong rental demand, making it one of the most attractive real estate markets connecting Europe and Asia. Districts like Beylikdüzü and Büyükçekmece are among the fastest-growing on the European side.

items.q: Can foreign nationals buy property in Turkey?
items.a: Yes. Citizens of most countries can freely purchase residential and commercial property in Turkey, subject to standard title deed procedures. Our team guides international buyers through every step.
HADARA offers flexible installment payment plans on select projects, in addition to standard cash purchase, making it easier for both residents and investors to secure a unit.

items.q: What costs should I budget for beyond the purchase price?
items.a: Typical additional costs include the title deed transfer fee, the appraisal report, and standard administrative charges. Our team will walk you through the full cost breakdown for any project you're interested in.

items.q: Is buying property in Turkey a good rental investment?
items.a: Istanbul's strong tourism and population growth support healthy rental demand, particularly in mixed-use and centrally located developments such as Lotus İstanbul.

categories.title: Turkish Citizenship by Real Estate Purchase

items.q: How can I obtain Turkish citizenship by buying property?
items.a: Turkey's citizenship-by-investment program allows foreign nationals who purchase qualifying real estate above a minimum value, and hold it for at least three years, to apply for Turkish citizenship.

items.q: What is the minimum investment amount required?
items.a: Under the current program rules, the minimum qualifying real estate investment is $400,000 USD (or equivalent). HADARA's team can confirm which of our projects meet this threshold.

items.q: Does citizenship extend to my family?
items.a: Yes. Your spouse and children under 18 are included in the same citizenship application at no additional investment.

items.q: How long does the process take?
items.a: After the property purchase and valuation report are completed, the citizenship application typically takes a few months to be reviewed and approved by the Turkish authorities.

items.q: Can I keep my current nationality?
items.a: Yes. Turkey permits dual citizenship for most nationalities, so you are not required to give up your original citizenship.

items.q: Do I need to live in Turkey to qualify?
items.a: No. There is no residency requirement before or after approval — you can maintain the property as an investment without relocating.

beylikduzu-living.shortDescription: Built on a 21,000 m² land area, Beylikdüzü Living offers a well-planned selection of residential units supported by comprehensive social amenities, creating a balanced environment for daily life.
beylikduzu-living.longDescription: Built on a 21,000 m² land area, Beylikdüzü Living offers a well-planned selection of residential units supported by comprehensive social amenities, creating a balanced environment for daily life. The community comprises 18 residential blocks around landscaped courtyards with a children's playground, sports court and walking track, offering 2+1 homes of about 100–109 m², 3+1 homes of 134–167 m² and spacious 4+1 homes of 194–197 m² gross, many with a dressing room, laundry room and generous balconies. With delivery scheduled for the end of 2028, the project stands as a strong choice for both comfortable living and sustainable investment in Istanbul.

diamond-marin.tagline: The jewel of the marina — boutique seaside living in Beylikdüzü.
diamond-marin.shortDescription: Diamond Marin is a boutique, low-rise residential project designed exclusively for 58 families in two blocks, just minutes from West Istanbul Marina and the sea.
diamond-marin.longDescription: Bringing the rhythm of the city together with the calm of the sea, Diamond Marin is a boutique, low-rise residential project in Beylikdüzü designed exclusively for 58 families across two blocks. Its elegant architecture, green surroundings and sea views are complemented by a private site concept with an outdoor swimming pool, fitness center, landscaped gardens, indoor car park and 24/7 private security. Every home is a spacious 3+1 apartment of 117.60 m² to 143.08 m² gross, with private garden terraces on the ground floor, and comes with a smart home system, built-in kitchen appliances, air conditioning, a combi boiler and heat and sound insulation. West Istanbul Marina and Beylikdüzü Yaşam Vadisi are 5 minutes away, the Metrobüs 10 minutes, MarmaraPark mall and Medicana International Istanbul Hospital 15 minutes, and Büyükçekmece beach 20 minutes. The project is developed in partnership by Yıltaş, active in construction for more than 40 years, and Lotus Yapı, the developer behind the Lotus projects. Delivery is scheduled for the end of 2027.

Developed by Lotus Yapı Proje, the project is complete and ready to move in, with a selection of villas still available for sale.

blog.heroSubtitle: Guides and insights on the Turkish property market, Istanbul, life in Turkey, and citizenship by real estate investment.

real-estate-in-turkey.title: Understanding the Turkish Real Estate Market
real-estate-in-turkey.excerpt: A practical look at what makes Turkey's property market attractive to both residents and international buyers.
body: Turkey's real estate market has grown steadily over the past decade, driven by a young population, rapid urbanization, and a strategic location bridging Europe and Asia. Istanbul remains the country's largest and most liquid market, with demand spread across residential, mixed-use and commercial segments.

For buyers, the market offers a wide range of options — from affordable apartments in emerging districts to premium residences and villas in established neighborhoods. Prices vary significantly by district, proximity to transport links, and the quality of construction and amenities.

Whether you're buying a home or an investment property, working with a developer who understands local regulations, construction standards and delivery timelines — like HADARA — makes the process considerably smoother from first viewing to final handover.

citizenship-by-real-estate.title: How Real Estate Investment Leads to Turkish Citizenship
citizenship-by-real-estate.excerpt: An overview of how buying qualifying property in Turkey can open the door to Turkish citizenship for you and your family.
body: Turkey's citizenship-by-investment program is one of the most accessible routes to a second citizenship worldwide. By purchasing real estate above the minimum investment threshold and holding it for at least three years, foreign nationals can apply for Turkish citizenship for themselves and their immediate family.
The appeal goes beyond the passport itself: investors gain exposure to a growing property market, rental income potential, and a foothold in a country connecting Europe, Asia and the Middle East.

The process involves property purchase, an official valuation report, and a citizenship application submitted to the relevant authorities. HADARA's team supports investors through each of these steps, from selecting a qualifying project to final approval.

about-turkey.title: Getting to Know Turkey: A Country Between Two Continents
about-turkey.excerpt: A brief introduction to Turkey's geography, economy and culture for prospective investors and residents.
body: Turkey spans two continents, with Istanbul itself straddling Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus. This unique position has shaped the country's history, culture and economy for centuries, making it a natural bridge for trade, travel and investment.

With a population of over 85 million and one of the world's largest emerging economies, Turkey combines a young, dynamic workforce with a growing middle class and expanding infrastructure — highways, airports, and metro lines connecting its major cities.

From the Mediterranean coastline to the mountains of Anatolia, Turkey's diversity extends well beyond Istanbul, but it is Istanbul's scale and connectivity that continues to draw the largest share of both residents and international investors.

about-istanbul.title: Istanbul: The City Where Continents Meet
about-istanbul.excerpt: Why Istanbul remains one of the most compelling cities for living, working and investing.
body: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city and its economic heart, home to over 15 million people. Its position on the Bosphorus, linking the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, has made it a center of trade and culture for thousands of years.

Today, Istanbul blends historic neighborhoods with rapidly developing districts like Beylikdüzü and Büyükçekmece on the European side, where new infrastructure, shopping centers and residential communities continue to reshape the skyline.

For residents, Istanbul offers a rare mix of history, culture, coastline and modern city life. For investors, its scale, connectivity and steady population growth continue to support long-term demand for both housing and rental properties.

life-in-turkey.title: What It's Like to Live in Turkey
life-in-turkey.excerpt: A look at daily life, cost of living and what to expect when settling in Turkey.
body: Life in Turkey combines a relaxed Mediterranean pace with the convenience of large modern cities. Turkish hospitality is well known, and most urban areas offer a comfortable blend of local culture and international amenities — from international schools to shopping malls and healthcare facilities.

Compared to many European countries, the cost of living in Turkey remains attractive, particularly for daily expenses such as groceries, dining out and transportation, while quality housing is available across a wide range of budgets.

For international residents, the growing presence of expat communities in areas like Beylikdüzü makes settling in easier, with many services — from banking to schooling — increasingly set up to support newcomers.

buying-property-and-tapu.title: How to Buy Property in Turkey and Register the Title Deed (Tapu)
buying-property-and-tapu.excerpt: A step-by-step look at the property purchase process, from reservation to receiving your Tapu.
body: Buying property in Turkey generally follows a clear sequence: selecting a unit, signing a reservation agreement, completing payment (in cash or installments), and finally transferring the title deed — known locally as the Tapu — at the Land Registry Office.

The Tapu is the official document proving ownership and is required for the property to be legally registered in the buyer's name. As part of the process, an official valuation report is prepared, and both parties (or their authorized representatives) attend the title deed office to finalize the transfer.

HADARA's team coordinates each of these steps on behalf of our buyers — from preparing the required documents to accompanying you or your representative to the Land Registry Office — so the transfer is completed correctly and on time.

taxes-and-tapu-fees.title: Understanding Property Tax and Title Deed (Tapu) Fees in Turkey
taxes-and-tapu-fees.excerpt: A clear breakdown of the taxes and fees to budget for when purchasing property in Turkey.
body: Beyond the purchase price, buyers should budget for a small number of standard fees. The most significant is the title deed (Tapu) transfer fee, which is calculated as a percentage of the property's declared value and is typically shared between buyer and seller.

Annual property tax is also payable to the local municipality once the property is registered, and is generally a modest percentage of the property's assessed value — far lower than property taxes in many other countries.

Additional costs may include the valuation report fee and standard administrative charges. Our team provides a full cost breakdown for any project before you commit, so there are no surprises during the purchase process.

real-estate-valuation.title: Why Real Estate Valuation Matters When Buying Property
real-estate-valuation.excerpt: What a property valuation report is, why it's required, and how it protects buyers.
body: A real estate valuation report is an official assessment of a property's market value, prepared by a licensed appraiser. In Turkey, this report is a mandatory step before the title deed transfer, and it is also required for foreign buyers applying for citizenship by investment.

The valuation considers factors such as location, construction quality, size, and comparable sales in the area, providing an objective benchmark that protects both buyer and seller from over- or under-valuation.

For investors, the valuation report also serves as an official record of the property's value at the time of purchase — useful documentation for future resale, financing, or the citizenship application process.

citizenship-investment-laws.title: Turkey's Citizenship-by-Investment Laws, Explained
citizenship-investment-laws.excerpt: The legal framework behind Turkey's citizenship-by-investment program, and what it means for buyers.
body: Turkey's citizenship-by-investment program is governed by regulations issued under Turkish citizenship law, which set out the qualifying investment routes — including real estate purchase above a minimum value — and the conditions applicants must meet.

Under current rules, a foreign national who purchases qualifying real estate and undertakes not to sell it for at least three years may apply for citizenship, along with a spouse and children under 18, without any additional investment.

Because these regulations can be updated by the Turkish government, it's important to work with a team that stays current on the requirements. HADARA's advisors confirm the latest thresholds and documentation requirements before you commit to a purchase.

real-estate-market-trends.title: Real Estate Trends Worth Watching in Istanbul
real-estate-market-trends.excerpt: A roundup of the trends shaping demand, pricing and design across Istanbul's growing districts.
body: Istanbul's real estate market continues to evolve, with demand increasingly concentrated in well-connected, master-planned districts that offer a mix of residential, retail and green space rather than standalone apartment blocks.
Mixed-use developments — combining homes, offices and retail in a single project — have grown in popularity, offering both residents and investors stronger rental potential and everyday convenience.

At the same time, buyers are placing more weight on construction quality, energy efficiency and social amenities than in previous years, a shift that continues to shape how developers like HADARA plan and deliver new projects.

privacy.heroSubtitle: How HADARA Real Estate handles information on this website.

sections.title: Who we are
paragraphs: This website is operated by HADARA Real Estate, Adnan Kahveci Mah., Beylikdüzü, Istanbul 34000, Türkiye. For any privacy question, write to info@byhadara.com.

sections.title: Anonymous visit statistics
paragraphs: To understand how many people visit the site and which projects interest them, our server records each page view anonymously. For each page we keep only:
items: the page address, without any query parameters;
the site language (English, Arabic, French or Russian);
where the visit came from — only the name of the referring website (for example google.com) or the previous page on our site, never the full link;
your approximate country and city, estimated by our hosting provider (Vercel) from your connection;
a random session number, and the date and time.
after: The session number is created by your browser and kept in its session storage (sessionStorage), only for the current tab. It is not a cookie, it is not linked to your name or device, and your browser deletes it when you close the tab.
We do not store your IP address or any personal information in these statistics, and we do not use them to identify anyone. Seller account and administration pages are not recorded.

Visit records are deleted automatically after 30 days. When a new visit starts, our team receives an internal notification (via Telegram) with the same anonymous details: approximate location, page, language and source.

sections.title: Information you send us
paragraphs: The contact, property request and consultation forms do not send anything to our servers: they open your own email app with a prepared message, and we receive only what you choose to send. The same applies when you contact us on WhatsApp or by phone.

If you create a seller account in the resale portal, we store the details you provide (name, email address, phone number, country of residence) and your listings and photos, so that we can review and publish them. Messages sent about a listing are stored so that we can reply to them.

sections.title: Booking a private video tour
paragraphs: When you book a private video tour, your appointment is recorded directly in our system, and we keep only:
items: your name, email address, phone number and preferred way of contact;
the time you chose, the projects and what you would like to see, the app and the tour language;
the site language, your time zone (to show the appointment in your local time) and the advertising source, if any;
the booking reference, date and status.
after: We use this information only to organise the tour and contact you about it: you receive a confirmation email, and our team receives an internal notification (by email and Telegram) with the booking details. Only our management team can see bookings.
Each booking is deleted automatically one year after the tour date, and you can ask us to delete it sooner by writing to info@byhadara.com

sections.title: Service providers
paragraphs: Our website is hosted by Vercel, and seller accounts, listings, tour bookings and visit statistics are stored with Supabase. Booking confirmation emails are sent through the email service Resend, and internal notifications are delivered through Telegram and email. If we use advertising or analytics tools from Meta or Google, they process data — and may use cookies — under their own privacy policies.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask us what information we hold about you, or ask us to correct or delete it, by writing to info@byhadara.com. Because the visit statistics contain nothing that identifies you, they cannot be linked to a specific person.

videoTour.visitTitle: When You Are Ready to Buy
videoTour.visitText: We always advise seeing the project in person before completing a purchase. The video tour helps you choose the right project and unit before you travel — and when you decide, we arrange your visit to Istanbul and accompany you at every step until you receive your title deed.

faq.a: Yes — the tour is completely free, with no obligation to buy.

faq.q: Do I need to install a new app?
faq.a: No. We use the app you already have: WhatsApp, FaceTime, Zoom or Google Meet. We call you directly or send you the call link.

faq.q: How long does the tour take?
faq.a: Usually 30 to 45 minutes; it can run longer depending on your questions and the number of projects you want to see.

faq.q: Can my family join the call?
faq.a: Of course — several people can join on Zoom, Google Meet or a WhatsApp group call.
Our advisors give the tour in Arabic, English and Turkish.

faq.q: What if I need to change the time?
faq.a: Reply to your confirmation email or message us on WhatsApp, and we will set a new time that suits you.

faq.q: Can I see more than one project in the same tour?
faq.a: Yes — choose every project you are interested in when booking and we will plan the tour so you see them all.

faq.q: Can I buy straight after the tour?
faq.a: We advise visiting Istanbul to see the project yourself before completing a purchase. The tour helps you decide what suits you before you travel, and we arrange your visit when you are ready.
